sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other species of the genus by the combination of nearly triangular ocelli in lateral view and a large fontanelle; the most similar species are O. heberi and O. longilamina, from which it differs in the ocelli being farther from the compound eyes. The soldier head capsule is larger than in O. brevipilosus, O. longilamina, O. macrocephalus and O. okeyma, with the sides of the head slightly convergent anteriorly, whereas they are parallel in O. gibberorum, O. heberi and O. orthognathus; it differs from O. uncimandibularis, whose left mandible ends in a strong hook.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes small, separated from the lower margin of the head by a distance equal to the greatest diameter of an ocellus. Ocelli kidney-shaped and narrow in dorsal view; nearly triangular in lateral view, separated from the compound eye by less than its least diameter. Fontanelle wide and large. Head capsule with short hairs, fewer ventrally, and scattered setae. Labral setae not arranged in rows. Pronotum densely covered with setae and short hairs; mesonotum and metanotum with short hairs, concentrated on the centre and the margins. Head dark brown, pronotum brown to dark brown, tergites brown to pale brown, sternites yellow, legs and wing scales pale brown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head slightly convergent anteriorly in dorsal view. Dorsal tubercle slightly prominent in lateral view, situated behind the lateral projection. Mandibles type 2, with a tooth-like process at the middle. Head capsule with short hairs and sparse setae, minute hairs scattered over the dorsum. Postmentum with setae and short hairs. Surface of the pronotum with short hairs and the margins with setae; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with setae; abdominal tergites densely covered with short hairs and setae, the sternites with short hairs and setae on the posterior margin.
